_comment: FIX-Task-63 — LEGACY OUT-OF-BAND EXCEPTION RECORD. These are staging schema changes that were applied with NO committed migration file behind them (MCP `apply_migration` calls, dashboard SQL, or an in-session adaptation that was never written back). The goal is NOT to rewrite history — it is to make every exception VISIBLE and TIME-BOUNDED, so a future one cannot hide inside a pile of unexplained ledger rows. `scripts/migrations/ledger-audit.mjs` prints these instead of reporting the rows as unmanaged, and flags any entry past its `expiresAt`.
_matchKeys: A row is explained if ANY of these matches: `ledgerName` / `ledgerNames[]` against the row's normalised `name`, or `ledgerVersion` against the row's `version`. Other keys are descriptive only — in particular `observedRowName` is NOT a match key, so an entry can record that a row's name is junk without whitelisting every row that shares that junk name.
_classRule: `ledgerNames` enumerates a MEASURED class instead of matching a pattern, so the entry expires with its evidence and a NEW row in that bucket still surfaces as unexplained APPLIED_ONLY drift. Every entry carries `doesNotCover` where the boundary is not obvious.

exceptions.reason: Ledger row whose `version` is an APPLY TIMESTAMP, not the filename prefix. The repo file is 20260918000009_fix_task_61_item_images_bucket_mime_alignment.sql and its effect was ALREADY live (allowed_mime_types contained heic/heif, file_size_limit 10485760) before the apply was requested. Provenance unresolved: a parallel session or a manual dashboard apply.

exceptions.reason: 31 ledger rows whose apply times run 2025-12-15 → 2026-09-14 and whose names exist as NO local file. This is NOT new drift: it is the same pre-existing population already measured on staging two days earlier, and its size has not moved except by one added file. It surfaced as 'unexplained' only because it was never written into this file. Names are ENUMERATED rather than pattern-matched, so the entry cannot absorb a future row.
exceptions.independentReference: supabase/migrations/README.md — FIX-Task-40 phase 3, measured 2026-09-16: "Staging's `schema_migrations` holds 266 rows whose `version` values are APPLY timestamps … 253 unique names, 32 with no local file at all, and 304 local files with no ledger row. A file-level attribution is therefore not derivable, so the binding test is that a creator exists in the chain." Re-measured 2026-09-18 (FIX-Task-64): 31 rows / 305 FILE_ONLY — the 32 → 31 and 304 → 305 deltas are the same single file added since; nothing about this class changed in character.
exceptions.reconciliationTask: FIX-Task-64 — record only. No re-apply and no backfill.
exceptions.reconciliation: not derivable at file level (established by the FIX-Task-40 measurement); recorded as one measured, named, expiring class instead of re-investigated per row
exceptions.doesNotCover: ONLY the 31 enumerated names, and only as they stand on 2026-09-18. Any ledger row that lands in this bucket AFTER that date does not match this entry and is still reported as unexplained APPLIED_ONLY drift — that is deliberate, and it is the point of enumerating names instead of matching a pattern.

exceptions.reason: Row identity is its VERSION, not its name. The stored name is the literal string `placeholder`, which several other rows also carry — keying this entry by name would whitelist all of them, including future ones. The file existed as supabase/migrations/20251217000001_seed_initial_nodes.sql (added 3087bf8e) and was RENAMED with zero content change in 5acfc7f4 (FIX-Task-42) to 20260916000083_seed_initial_nodes.sql, which is present and committed today. The ledger row is the historical apply of a file that still exists under a different number, so it is not drift.
